correctness.rationale: Hare sorts any binary segment, since splitting at all maximal 1s leaves only zeros. Splitting a ternary input at its k copies of 2 gives k+1 such segments and moves the 2s to the end. Therefore each 10 in the binary prefix of an output must cross a segment boundary and there are at most k. Conversely the cuts at all 10s produce nondecreasing pieces; pad with empty pieces, then interleave k separators. This includes the empty prefix and the k=0 binary case. The ordered weak cuts are unique for the segment lengths of any one input, and choosing each segment with its prescribed counts gives the product of binomial coefficients, so summation neither omits nor duplicates inputs. A deterministic machine increments for 10 and decrements (saturating at zero) on the final 2-block, using finite state for phase and previous symbol and accepting at counter zero. Appending 2^i separates (10)^i and (10)^j for i<j. A prefix with d descents has 2d mandatory run letters in 2d+2 run exponents, giving z^(2d)/(1−z)^(2d+2) and the stated binomial counts. The terminal block contributes z^d/(1−z), yielding the rational series; its denominator expands to 1−3z+3z²−2z³+z⁴, giving the recurrence. For λ(λ−1)²=1 there is just one real root (the local maximum on [0,1] is 4/27 and negative λ cannot solve it). The other reciprocal roots have modulus λ^(−1/2) by the conjugate-pair product. The coefficient of (1−z/r)⁻¹ is −1/[r(1−r)q′(r)] for q(z)=(1−z)²−z³, agreeing with the given constant; division by 3^n gives exponential decay.
residual_risks: The finite replay is a consistency check; the classification and asymptotic for arbitrary n depend on the combinatorial and analytic proofs. Only one pass and the fixed ternary alphabet are covered.
